analysis:
Only docs/developer/build.md head text was supplied, with no patch or base side, so I could not isolate the changed lines. I read both units in full and found no concrete security regression. The file is build and CI documentation only.

Security-relevant statements, none of which change controls:
- Line 257 describes official-build registration through the scoped POST /v1/releases. It says no per-release hardware qualification or manual approval is required, and that retries reuse the original signed artifact. This matches the canonical A-005, A-011, A-017 and T-054 context, which already puts release publication and durable qualification in scope.
- Lines 259-263 say secret-bearing release jobs accept only verified signed annotated tags in reviewed master ancestry, or trusted master for dev/manual/recovery runs. They add that this assumes trusted repository writers and that CI establishes official identity, not runtime Apple success. This is an explicit assumption. The release supply chain is out of scope, so no threat-model gap follows.
- Lines 334-337 say protected signing and publication jobs keep their existing approvals. Line 262 says release jobs have no environment approval attachments. The wording is slightly ambiguous, but it is documentation and I treated it as non-actionable.
- Lines 116-124 and 109-114 describe pinned, SHA-256-verified installer and GitHub CLI downloads. This is a hardening description.
- Lines 71-79 say the CI component detector fails on missing revisions rather than skipping jobs, and that docs-only changes skip builds. This is not a security gate.
- Lines 366-398 say caches hold only unsigned build products, never signing keys.

No provider, coordinator or wire code changed in the supplied units. The T-053, T-054 and T-057 behaviours are unchanged. No integration follow-ups are needed beyond confirming the real workflow and script files match the described gates, since they were not supplied.
